notes:
ADVERSARIAL READ vs /images/blueprints/remote/da407a0ce211__3406.jpg.

WHAT THE DRAWING SPECIFIES: the trouser front with the fly closed. The red line runs along the top edge of the waistband, then turns down at the fly and follows the fly edge, with the turn happening at a distinct angular step rather than a curve — the 'pointed' finish where the fly meets the waistband.

DISCRIMINATION CHECK AGAINST THE SIBLING. 'Fish-Claw Fly' (3402) was generated in the same run from the same trouser template, so I cropped both renders and compared them side by side at 3x. This one shows the fly's topstitched edge rising to an ANGULAR apex under the waistband; the sibling shows a large rounded lobe curling over the waistband. Two clearly different geometries, which is exactly what these two assets have to deliver.

ATTEMPTED REJECTIONS THAT FAILED:
(1) Did it render the sibling's rounded claw by mistake? No — the apex is angular, formed by two straight runs of edge stitching meeting.
(2) Square-ended fly, the default finish? No — the edge rises to a peak rather than stopping square.
(3) Fly open? No — closed and pressed, as drawn.
(4) Annotation traced from the red line along the waistband? No — no red, no line along the waistband top, no numbers.
(5) Wrong face or region? Trouser front, waistband and fly. Correct.

Two minor findings, logged above. No critical or major findings.
